15 /-!
16 # Simple graphs
17 
18 This module defines simple graphs on a vertex type `V` as an irreflexive symmetric relation.
19 
20 ## Main definitions
21 
22 * `SimpleGraph` is a structure for symmetric, irreflexive relations.
23 
24 * `SimpleGraph.neighborSet` is the `Set` of vertices adjacent to a given vertex.
25 
26 * `SimpleGraph.commonNeighbors` is the intersection of the neighbor sets of two given vertices.
27 
28 * `SimpleGraph.incidenceSet` is the `Set` of edges containing a given vertex.
29 
30 * `CompleteAtomicBooleanAlgebra` instance: Under the subgraph relation, `SimpleGraph` forms a
31   `CompleteAtomicBooleanAlgebra`. In other words, this is the complete lattice of spanning subgraphs
32   of the complete graph.
33 
34 ## TODO
35 
36 * This is the simplest notion of an unoriented graph.
37   This should eventually fit into a more complete combinatorics hierarchy which includes
38   multigraphs and directed graphs.
39   We begin with simple graphs in order to start learning what the combinatorics hierarchy should
40   look like.
41 -/

48 /--
49 A variant of the `aesop` tactic for use in the graph library. Changes relative
50 to standard `aesop`:
51 
52 - We use the `SimpleGraph` rule set in addition to the default rule sets.
53 - We instruct Aesop's `intro` rule to unfold with `default` transparency.
54 - We instruct Aesop to fail if it can't fully solve the goal. This allows us to
55   use `aesop_graph` for auto-params.
56 -/
57 macro (name := aesop_graph) "aesop_graph" c:Aesop.tactic_clause* : tactic =>
58   `(tactic|
59     aesop $c*
60       (config := { introsTransparency? := some .default, terminal := true })
61       (rule_sets := [$(Lean.mkIdent `SimpleGraph):ident]))
62 
63 /--
64 Use `aesop_graph?` to pass along a `Try this` suggestion when using `aesop_graph`
65 -/
66 macro (name := aesop_graph?) "aesop_graph?" c:Aesop.tactic_clause* : tactic =>
67   `(tactic|
68     aesop? $c*
69       (config := { introsTransparency? := some .default, terminal := true })
70       (rule_sets := [$(Lean.mkIdent `SimpleGraph):ident]))
71 
72 /--
73 A variant of `aesop_graph` which does not fail if it is unable to solve the goal.
74 Use this only for exploration! Nonterminal Aesop is even worse than nonterminal `simp`.
75 -/
76 macro (name := aesop_graph_nonterminal) "aesop_graph_nonterminal" c:Aesop.tactic_clause* : tactic =>
77   `(tactic|
78     aesop $c*
79       (config := { introsTransparency? := some .default, warnOnNonterminal := false })
80       (rule_sets := [$(Lean.mkIdent `SimpleGraph):ident]))

86 /-- A simple graph is an irreflexive symmetric relation `Adj` on a vertex type `V`.
87 The relation describes which pairs of vertices are adjacent.
88 There is exactly one edge for every pair of adjacent vertices;
89 see `SimpleGraph.edgeSet` for the corresponding edge set.
90 -/
91 @[ext, aesop safe constructors (rule_sets := [SimpleGraph])]
92 structure SimpleGraph (V : Type u) where
93   /-- The adjacency relation of a simple graph. -/
94   Adj : V → V → Prop
95   symm : Symmetric Adj := by aesop_graph
96   loopless : Std.Irrefl Adj := by aesop_graph
97 
98 initialize_simps_projections SimpleGraph (Adj → adj)
99 
100 /-- Constructor for simple graphs using a symmetric irreflexive Boolean function. -/
101 @[simps]
102 def SimpleGraph.mk' {V : Type u} :
103     {adj : V → V → Bool // (∀ x y, adj x y = adj y x) ∧ (∀ x, ¬ adj x x)} ↪ SimpleGraph V where
104   toFun x := ⟨fun v w ↦ x.1 v w, fun v w ↦ by simp [x.2.1], ⟨fun v ↦ by simp [x.2.2]⟩⟩
105   inj' := by
106     rintro ⟨adj, _⟩ ⟨adj', _⟩
107     simp only [mk.injEq, Subtype.mk.injEq]
108     intro h
109     funext v w
110     simpa [Bool.coe_iff_coe] using congr_fun₂ h v w
111 
112 /-- We can enumerate simple graphs by enumerating all functions `V → V → Bool`
113 and filtering on whether they are symmetric and irreflexive. -/
114 instance {V : Type u} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] : Fintype (SimpleGraph V) where
115   elems := Finset.univ.map SimpleGraph.mk'
116   complete := by
117     classical
118     rintro ⟨Adj, hs, hi⟩
119     simp only [mem_map, mem_univ, true_and, Subtype.exists, Bool.not_eq_true]
120     refine ⟨fun v w ↦ Adj v w, ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
121     · simp [hs.iff]
122     · intro v; simp [hi.irrefl v]
123     · ext
124       simp
125 
126 /-- There are finitely many simple graphs on a given finite type. -/
127 instance SimpleGraph.instFinite {V : Type u} [Finite V] : Finite (SimpleGraph V) :=
128   .of_injective SimpleGraph.Adj fun _ _ ↦ SimpleGraph.ext
129 
130 /-- Construct the simple graph induced by the given relation. It
131 symmetrizes the relation and makes it irreflexive. -/
132 def SimpleGraph.fromRel {V : Type u} (r : V → V → Prop) : SimpleGraph V where
133   Adj a b := a ≠ b ∧ (r a b ∨ r b a)
134   symm := fun _ _ ⟨hn, hr⟩ => ⟨hn.symm, hr.symm⟩
135   loopless := ⟨fun _ ⟨hn, _⟩ => hn rfl⟩
136 
137 @[simp]
138 theorem SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj {V : Type u} (r : V → V → Prop) (v w : V) :
139     (SimpleGraph.fromRel r).Adj v w ↔ v ≠ w ∧ (r v w ∨ r w v) :=
140   Iff.rfl
141 
142 attribute [aesop safe (rule_sets := [SimpleGraph])] Ne.symm
143 attribute [aesop safe (rule_sets := [SimpleGraph])] Ne.irrefl
144 
145 instance {V : Type u} [DecidableEq V] (r : V → V → Prop)
146     [DecidableRel r] : DecidableRel (SimpleGraph.fromRel r).Adj :=
147   inferInstanceAs (DecidableRel fun a b ↦ a ≠ b ∧ (r a b ∨ r b a))
148 
149 /-- Two vertices are adjacent in the complete bipartite graph on two vertex types
150 if and only if they are not from the same side.
151 Any bipartite graph may be regarded as a subgraph of one of these. -/
152 @[simps]
153 def completeBipartiteGraph (V W : Type*) : SimpleGraph (V ⊕ W) where
154   Adj v w := v.isLeft ∧ w.isRight ∨ v.isRight ∧ w.isLeft
155   symm v w := by cases v <;> cases w <;> simp
156   loopless := ⟨fun v ↦ by cases v <;> simp⟩
157

162 @[simp]
163 protected theorem irrefl {v : V} : ¬G.Adj v v :=
164   G.loopless.irrefl v
165 
166 theorem adj_comm (u v : V) : G.Adj u v ↔ G.Adj v u :=
167   ⟨fun x => G.symm x, fun x => G.symm x⟩
168 
169 @[symm]
170 theorem adj_symm (h : G.Adj u v) : G.Adj v u :=
171   G.symm h
172 
173 theorem Adj.symm {G : SimpleGraph V} {u v : V} (h : G.Adj u v) : G.Adj v u :=
174   G.symm h
175 
176 theorem ne_of_adj (h : G.Adj a b) : a ≠ b := by
177   rintro rfl
178   exact G.irrefl h
179 
180 protected theorem Adj.ne {G : SimpleGraph V} {a b : V} (h : G.Adj a b) : a ≠ b :=
181   G.ne_of_adj h
182 
183 protected theorem Adj.ne' {G : SimpleGraph V} {a b : V} (h : G.Adj a b) : b ≠ a :=
184   h.ne.symm
185 
186 theorem ne_of_adj_of_not_adj {v w x : V} (h : G.Adj v x) (hn : ¬G.Adj w x) : v ≠ w := fun h' =>
187   hn (h' ▸ h)
188 
189 theorem adj_injective : Injective (Adj : SimpleGraph V → V → V → Prop) :=
190   fun _ _ => SimpleGraph.ext
191 
192 @[simp]
193 theorem adj_inj {G H : SimpleGraph V} : G.Adj = H.Adj ↔ G = H :=
194   adj_injective.eq_iff
195 
196 theorem adj_congr_of_sym2 {u v w x : V} (h : s(u, v) = s(w, x)) : G.Adj u v ↔ G.Adj w x := by
197   simp only [Sym2.eq, Sym2.rel_iff', Prod.mk.injEq, Prod.swap_prod_mk] at h
198   rcases h with hl | hr
199   · rw [hl.1, hl.2]
200   · rw [hr.1, hr.2, adj_comm]
201 
202 instance symm_adj (f : ι → V) : Std.Symm fun i j ↦ G.Adj (f i) (f j) where symm _ _ := .symm

206 /-- The relation that one `SimpleGraph` is a subgraph of another.
207 Note that this should be spelled `≤`. -/
208 @[deprecated "use `≤` instead" (since := "2026-03-25")]
209 def IsSubgraph (x y : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
210   ∀ ⦃v w : V⦄, x.Adj v w → y.Adj v w
211 
212 /-- For graphs `G`, `H`, `G ≤ H` iff `∀ a b, G.Adj a b → H.Adj a b`. -/
213 instance : LE (SimpleGraph V) where
214   le x y := ∀ ⦃v w : V⦄, x.Adj v w → y.Adj v w
215 
216 lemma le_iff_adj {G H : SimpleGraph V} : G ≤ H ↔ ∀ v w, G.Adj v w → H.Adj v w := .rfl
217 
218 /-- The supremum of two graphs `x ⊔ y` has edges where either `x` or `y` have edges. -/
219 instance : Max (SimpleGraph V) where
220   max x y :=
221     { Adj := x.Adj ⊔ y.Adj
222       symm := fun v w h => by rwa [Pi.sup_apply, Pi.sup_apply, x.adj_comm, y.adj_comm] }
223 
224 @[simp]
225 theorem sup_adj (x y : SimpleGraph V) (v w : V) : (x ⊔ y).Adj v w ↔ x.Adj v w ∨ y.Adj v w :=
226   Iff.rfl
227 
228 /-- The infimum of two graphs `x ⊓ y` has edges where both `x` and `y` have edges. -/
229 instance : Min (SimpleGraph V) where
230   min x y :=
231     { Adj := x.Adj ⊓ y.Adj
232       symm := fun v w h => by rwa [Pi.inf_apply, Pi.inf_apply, x.adj_comm, y.adj_comm] }
233 
234 @[simp]
235 theorem inf_adj (x y : SimpleGraph V) (v w : V) : (x ⊓ y).Adj v w ↔ x.Adj v w ∧ y.Adj v w :=
236   Iff.rfl
237 
238 /-- We define `Gᶜ` to be the `SimpleGraph V` such that no two adjacent vertices in `G`
239 are adjacent in the complement, and every nonadjacent pair of vertices is adjacent
240 (still ensuring that vertices are not adjacent to themselves). -/
241 instance : Compl (SimpleGraph V) where
242   compl G :=
243     { Adj := fun v w => v ≠ w ∧ ¬G.Adj v w
244       symm := fun v w ⟨hne, _⟩ => ⟨hne.symm, by rwa [adj_comm]⟩
245       loopless := ⟨fun _ ⟨hne, _⟩ => (hne rfl).elim⟩ }
246 
247 @[simp]
248 theorem compl_adj (G : SimpleGraph V) (v w : V) : Gᶜ.Adj v w ↔ v ≠ w ∧ ¬G.Adj v w :=
249   Iff.rfl
250 
251 /-- The difference of two graphs `x \ y` has the edges of `x` with the edges of `y` removed. -/
252 instance sdiff : SDiff (SimpleGraph V) where
253   sdiff x y :=
254     { Adj := x.Adj \ y.Adj
255       symm := fun v w h => by change x.Adj w v ∧ ¬y.Adj w v; rwa [x.adj_comm, y.adj_comm] }
256 
257 @[simp]
258 theorem sdiff_adj (x y : SimpleGraph V) (v w : V) : (x \ y).Adj v w ↔ x.Adj v w ∧ ¬y.Adj v w :=
259   Iff.rfl
260 
261 instance supSet : SupSet (SimpleGraph V) where
262   sSup s :=
263     { Adj := fun a b => ∃ G ∈ s, Adj G a b
264       symm := fun _ _ => Exists.imp fun _ => And.imp_right Adj.symm
265       loopless := ⟨fun _ ⟨_, _, ha⟩ ↦ ha.ne rfl⟩ }
266 
267 instance infSet : InfSet (SimpleGraph V) where
268   sInf s :=
269     { Adj := fun a b => (∀ ⦃G⦄, G ∈ s → Adj G a b) ∧ a ≠ b
270       symm := fun _ _ => And.imp (forall₂_imp fun _ _ => Adj.symm) Ne.symm
271       loopless := ⟨fun _ h => h.2 rfl⟩ }
272 
273 @[simp]
274 theorem sSup_adj {s : Set (SimpleGraph V)} {a b : V} : (sSup s).Adj a b ↔ ∃ G ∈ s, Adj G a b :=
275   Iff.rfl
276 
277 @[simp]
278 theorem sInf_adj {s : Set (SimpleGraph V)} : (sInf s).Adj a b ↔ (∀ G ∈ s, Adj G a b) ∧ a ≠ b :=
279   Iff.rfl
280 
281 @[simp]
282 theorem iSup_adj {f : ι → SimpleGraph V} : (⨆ i, f i).Adj a b ↔ ∃ i, (f i).Adj a b := by simp [iSup]
283 
284 @[simp]
285 theorem iInf_adj {f : ι → SimpleGraph V} : (⨅ i, f i).Adj a b ↔ (∀ i, (f i).Adj a b) ∧ a ≠ b := by
286   simp [iInf]
287 
288 theorem sInf_adj_of_nonempty {s : Set (SimpleGraph V)} (hs : s.Nonempty) :
289     (sInf s).Adj a b ↔ ∀ G ∈ s, Adj G a b :=
290   sInf_adj.trans <|
291     and_iff_left_of_imp <| by
292       obtain ⟨G, hG⟩ := hs
293       exact fun h => (h _ hG).ne
294 
295 theorem iInf_adj_of_nonempty [Nonempty ι] {f : ι → SimpleGraph V} :
296     (⨅ i, f i).Adj a b ↔ ∀ i, (f i).Adj a b := by
297   rw [iInf, sInf_adj_of_nonempty (Set.range_nonempty _), Set.forall_mem_range]
298 
299 instance : PartialOrder (SimpleGraph V) :=
300   fast_instance% PartialOrder.lift _ adj_injective
301 
302 instance distribLattice : DistribLattice (SimpleGraph V) :=
303   adj_injective.distribLattice _ .rfl .rfl (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) fun _ _ ↦ rfl
304 
305 instance completeAtomicBooleanAlgebra : CompleteAtomicBooleanAlgebra (SimpleGraph V) where
306   top.Adj := Ne
307   bot.Adj _ _ := False
308   le_top x _ _ h := x.ne_of_adj h
309   bot_le _ _ _ h := h.elim
310   sdiff_eq x y := by
311     ext v w
312     refine ⟨fun h => ⟨h.1, ⟨?_, h.2⟩⟩, fun h => ⟨h.1, h.2.2⟩⟩
313     rintro rfl
314     exact x.irrefl h.1
315   inf_compl_le_bot _ _ _ h := False.elim <| h.2.2 h.1
316   top_le_sup_compl G v w hvw := by
317     by_cases h : G.Adj v w
318     · exact Or.inl h
319     · exact Or.inr ⟨hvw, h⟩
320   isLUB_sSup _ := ⟨fun G hG _ _ hab ↦ ⟨G, hG, hab⟩, fun _ hG _ _ ⟨_, hH, hab⟩ ↦ hG hH hab⟩
321   isGLB_sInf _ := ⟨fun _ hG _ _ hab ↦ hab.1 hG, fun _ hG _ _ hab ↦ ⟨fun _ hH => hG hH hab, hab.ne⟩⟩
322   iInf_iSup_eq f := by ext; simp [Classical.skolem]

324 /-- The complete graph on a type `V` is the simple graph with all pairs of distinct vertices. -/
325 abbrev completeGraph (V : Type u) : SimpleGraph V := ⊤
326 
327 /-- The graph with no edges on a given vertex type `V`. -/
328 abbrev emptyGraph (V : Type u) : SimpleGraph V := ⊥
329 
330 @[simp]
331 theorem top_adj (v w : V) : (⊤ : SimpleGraph V).Adj v w ↔ v ≠ w :=
332   Iff.rfl
333 
334 @[simp]
335 theorem bot_adj (v w : V) : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).Adj v w ↔ False :=
336   Iff.rfl
337 
338 @[simp]
339 theorem completeGraph_eq_top (V : Type u) : completeGraph V = ⊤ :=
340   rfl
341 
342 @[simp]
343 theorem emptyGraph_eq_bot (V : Type u) : emptyGraph V = ⊥ :=
344   rfl

346 variable {G}
347 
348 theorem eq_bot_iff_forall_not_adj : G = ⊥ ↔ ∀ a b : V, ¬G.Adj a b := by
349   simp [← le_bot_iff, le_iff_adj]
350 
351 theorem ne_bot_iff_exists_adj : G ≠ ⊥ ↔ ∃ a b : V, G.Adj a b := by
352   simp [eq_bot_iff_forall_not_adj]
353 
354 theorem eq_top_iff_forall_ne_adj : G = ⊤ ↔ ∀ a b : V, a ≠ b → G.Adj a b := by
355   simp [← top_le_iff, le_iff_adj]
356 
357 theorem ne_top_iff_exists_not_adj : G ≠ ⊤ ↔ ∃ a b : V, a ≠ b ∧ ¬G.Adj a b := by
358   simp [eq_top_iff_forall_ne_adj]

402 /-- `G.support` is the set of vertices that form edges in `G`. -/
403 def support : Set V :=
404   SetRel.dom {(u, v) : V × V | G.Adj u v}
405 
406 theorem mem_support {v : V} : v ∈ G.support ↔ ∃ w, G.Adj v w :=
407   Iff.rfl
408 
409 theorem support_mono {G G' : SimpleGraph V} (h : G ≤ G') : G.support ⊆ G'.support :=
410   SetRel.dom_mono fun _uv huv ↦ h huv
411 
412 /-- All vertices are in the support of the complete graph if there is more than one vertex. -/
413 @[simp]
414 theorem support_top_of_nontrivial [Nontrivial V] : (⊤ : SimpleGraph V).support = Set.univ :=
415   Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun v₁ => exists_ne v₁ |>.imp fun _v₂ h => h.symm
416 
417 /-- The support of the empty graph is empty. -/
418 @[simp]
419 theorem support_bot : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).support = ∅ :=
420   SetRel.dom_eq_empty_iff.mpr <| Set.empty_def.symm
421 
422 /-- Only the empty graph has empty support. -/
423 @[simp]
424 theorem support_eq_bot_iff : G.support = ∅ ↔ G = ⊥ :=
425   ⟨fun h ↦ eq_bot_iff_forall_not_adj.mpr fun v w nadj ↦
426     Set.ext_iff.mp (SetRel.dom_eq_empty_iff.mp h) (v, w) |>.mp nadj |>.elim,
427    (· ▸ support_bot)⟩
428 
429 /-- The support of a graph is empty if there at most one vertex. -/
430 @[simp]
431 theorem support_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton V] : G.support = ∅ :=
432   uniqueOfSubsingleton.uniq G ▸ support_bot
433 
434 /-- `G.neighborSet v` is the set of vertices adjacent to `v` in `G`. -/
435 def neighborSet (v : V) : Set V := {w | G.Adj v w}
436 
437 instance neighborSet.memDecidable (v : V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
438     DecidablePred (· ∈ G.neighborSet v) :=
439   inferInstanceAs <| DecidablePred (Adj G v)
440 
441 lemma neighborSet_subset_support (v : V) : G.neighborSet v ⊆ G.support :=
442   fun _ hadj ↦ ⟨v, hadj.symm⟩
443 
444 section EdgeSet
445 
446 variable {G₁ G₂ : SimpleGraph V}
447 
448 /-- The edges of G consist of the unordered pairs of vertices related by
449 `G.Adj`. This is the order embedding; for the edge set of a particular graph, see
450 `SimpleGraph.edgeSet`.
451 
452 The way `edgeSet` is defined is such that `mem_edgeSet` is proved by `Iff.rfl`.
453 (That is, `s(v, w) ∈ G.edgeSet` is definitionally equal to `G.Adj v w`.)
454 -/
455 -- Porting note: We need a separate definition so that dot notation works.
456 def edgeSetEmbedding (V : Type*) : SimpleGraph V ↪o Set (Sym2 V) :=
457   OrderEmbedding.ofMapLEIff (fun G => Sym2.fromRel G.symm) fun _ _ =>
458     ⟨fun h a b => @h s(a, b), fun h e => Sym2.ind @h e⟩
459 
460 /-- `G.edgeSet` is the edge set for `G`.
461 This is an abbreviation for `edgeSetEmbedding G` that permits dot notation. -/
462 abbrev edgeSet (G : SimpleGraph V) : Set (Sym2 V) := edgeSetEmbedding V G
463 
464 @[simp]
465 theorem mem_edgeSet : s(v, w) ∈ G.edgeSet ↔ G.Adj v w :=
466   Iff.rfl
467 
468 theorem not_isDiag_of_mem_edgeSet : e ∈ edgeSet G → ¬e.IsDiag :=
469   Sym2.ind (fun _ _ => Adj.ne) e
470 
471 @[simp] lemma not_mem_edgeSet_of_isDiag : e.IsDiag → e ∉ edgeSet G :=
472   imp_not_comm.1 G.not_isDiag_of_mem_edgeSet
473 
474 alias _root_.Sym2.IsDiag.not_mem_edgeSet := not_mem_edgeSet_of_isDiag
475 
476 theorem edgeSet_inj : G₁.edgeSet = G₂.edgeSet ↔ G₁ = G₂ := (edgeSetEmbedding V).eq_iff_eq
477 
478 @[simp]
479 theorem edgeSet_subset_edgeSet : edgeSet G₁ ⊆ edgeSet G₂ ↔ G₁ ≤ G₂ :=
480   (edgeSetEmbedding V).le_iff_le
481 
482 @[simp]
483 theorem edgeSet_ssubset_edgeSet : edgeSet G₁ ⊂ edgeSet G₂ ↔ G₁ < G₂ :=
484   (edgeSetEmbedding V).lt_iff_lt
485 
486 theorem edgeSet_injective : Injective (edgeSet : SimpleGraph V → Set (Sym2 V)) :=
487   (edgeSetEmbedding V).injective
488 
489 @[gcongr] alias ⟨_, edgeSet_mono⟩ := edgeSet_subset_edgeSet
490 
491 @[gcongr] alias ⟨_, edgeSet_strict_mono⟩ := edgeSet_ssubset_edgeSet
492 
493 attribute [mono] edgeSet_mono edgeSet_strict_mono
494 
495 variable (G₁ G₂)
496 
497 @[simp]
498 theorem edgeSet_bot : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet = ∅ :=
499   Sym2.fromRel_bot
500 
501 @[simp]
502 theorem edgeSet_top : (⊤ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet = Sym2.diagSetᶜ :=
503   Sym2.diagSet_compl_eq_fromRel_ne.symm
504 
505 @[simp]
506 theorem edgeSet_subset_compl_diagSet : G.edgeSet ⊆ Sym2.diagSetᶜ := by
507   simpa [Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_left, edgeSet, edgeSetEmbedding] using G.loopless
508 
509 @[deprecated (since := "2025-12-10")]
510 alias edgeSet_subset_setOf_not_isDiag := edgeSet_subset_compl_diagSet
511 
512 @[simp]
513 theorem edgeSet_sup : (G₁ ⊔ G₂).edgeSet = G₁.edgeSet ∪ G₂.edgeSet := by
514   ext ⟨x, y⟩
515   rfl
516 
517 @[simp]
518 theorem edgeSet_inf : (G₁ ⊓ G₂).edgeSet = G₁.edgeSet ∩ G₂.edgeSet := by
519   ext ⟨x, y⟩
520   rfl
521 
522 @[simp]
523 theorem edgeSet_sdiff : (G₁ \ G₂).edgeSet = G₁.edgeSet \ G₂.edgeSet := by
524   ext ⟨x, y⟩
525   rfl
526 
527 variable {G G₁ G₂}
528 
529 @[simp] lemma disjoint_edgeSet : Disjoint G₁.edgeSet G₂.edgeSet ↔ Disjoint G₁ G₂ := by
530   rw [Set.disjoint_iff, disjoint_iff_inf_le, ← edgeSet_inf, ← edgeSet_bot, ← Set.le_iff_subset,
531     OrderEmbedding.le_iff_le]
532 
533 @[simp] lemma edgeSet_eq_empty : G.edgeSet = ∅ ↔ G = ⊥ := by rw [← edgeSet_bot, edgeSet_inj]
534 
535 @[simp] lemma edgeSet_nonempty : G.edgeSet.Nonempty ↔ G ≠ ⊥ := by
536   rw [Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty, edgeSet_eq_empty.ne]
537 
538 /-- This lemma, combined with `edgeSet_sdiff` and `edgeSet_fromEdgeSet`,
539 allows proving `(G \ fromEdgeSet s).edgeSet = G.edgeSet \ s` by `simp`. -/
540 @[simp]
541 theorem edgeSet_sdiff_sdiff_isDiag (G : SimpleGraph V) (s : Set (Sym2 V)) :
542     G.edgeSet \ (s \ Sym2.diagSet) = G.edgeSet \ s := by
543   grind [Sym2.mem_diagSet, not_isDiag_of_mem_edgeSet]
544 
545 /-- Two vertices are adjacent iff there is an edge between them. The
546 condition `v ≠ w` ensures they are different endpoints of the edge,
547 which is necessary since when `v = w` the existential
548 `∃ (e ∈ G.edgeSet), v ∈ e ∧ w ∈ e` is satisfied by every edge
549 incident to `v`. -/
550 theorem adj_iff_exists_edge {v w : V} : G.Adj v w ↔ v ≠ w ∧ ∃ e ∈ G.edgeSet, v ∈ e ∧ w ∈ e := by
551   refine ⟨fun _ => ⟨G.ne_of_adj ‹_›, s(v, w), by simpa⟩, ?_⟩
552   rintro ⟨hne, e, he, hv⟩
553   rw [Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff hne] at hv
554   subst e
555   rwa [mem_edgeSet] at he
556 
557 theorem adj_iff_exists_edge_coe : G.Adj a b ↔ ∃ e : G.edgeSet, e.val = s(a, b) := by
558   simp only [mem_edgeSet, exists_prop, SetCoe.exists, exists_eq_right]
559 
560 variable (G G₁ G₂)
561 
562 theorem edge_other_ne {e : Sym2 V} (he : e ∈ G.edgeSet) {v : V} (h : v ∈ e) :
563     Sym2.Mem.other h ≠ v := by
564   rw [← Sym2.other_spec h, Sym2.eq_swap] at he
565   exact G.ne_of_adj he
566 
567 instance decidableMemEdgeSet [DecidableRel G.Adj] : DecidablePred (· ∈ G.edgeSet) :=
568   Sym2.fromRel.decidablePred G.symm
569 
570 instance fintypeEdgeSet [Fintype (Sym2 V)] [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Fintype G.edgeSet :=
571   Subtype.fintype _
572 
573 instance fintypeEdgeSetBot : Fintype (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet := by
574   rw [edgeSet_bot]
575   infer_instance
576 
577 instance fintypeEdgeSetSup [DecidableEq V] [Fintype G₁.edgeSet] [Fintype G₂.edgeSet] :
578     Fintype (G₁ ⊔ G₂).edgeSet := by
579   rw [edgeSet_sup]
580   infer_instance
581 
582 instance fintypeEdgeSetInf [DecidableEq V] [Fintype G₁.edgeSet] [Fintype G₂.edgeSet] :
583     Fintype (G₁ ⊓ G₂).edgeSet := by
584   rw [edgeSet_inf]
585   exact Set.fintypeInter _ _
586 
587 instance fintypeEdgeSetSdiff [DecidableEq V] [Fintype G₁.edgeSet] [Fintype G₂.edgeSet] :
588     Fintype (G₁ \ G₂).edgeSet := by
589   rw [edgeSet_sdiff]
590   exact Set.fintypeDiff _ _
591 
592 end EdgeSet

594 section FromEdgeSet
595 
596 variable (s : Set (Sym2 V))
597 
598 /-- `fromEdgeSet` constructs a `SimpleGraph` from a set of edges, without loops. -/
599 def fromEdgeSet : SimpleGraph V where
600   Adj := Sym2.ToRel s ⊓ Ne
601   symm _ _ h := ⟨Sym2.toRel_symmetric s h.1, h.2.symm⟩
602 
603 instance [DecidablePred (· ∈ s)] [DecidableEq V] : DecidableRel (fromEdgeSet s).Adj :=
604   inferInstanceAs <| DecidableRel fun v w ↦ s(v, w) ∈ s ∧ v ≠ w
605 
606 @[simp]
607 theorem fromEdgeSet_adj : (fromEdgeSet s).Adj v w ↔ s(v, w) ∈ s ∧ v ≠ w :=
608   Iff.rfl
609 
610 -- Note: we need to make sure `fromEdgeSet_adj` and this lemma are confluent.
611 -- In particular, both yield `s(u, v) ∈ (fromEdgeSet s).edgeSet` ==> `s(v, w) ∈ s ∧ v ≠ w`.
612 @[simp]
613 theorem edgeSet_fromEdgeSet : (fromEdgeSet s).edgeSet = s \ Sym2.diagSet := by
614   ext e
615   exact Sym2.ind (by simp) e
616 
617 @[simp]
618 theorem fromEdgeSet_edgeSet : fromEdgeSet G.edgeSet = G := by
619   ext v w
620   exact ⟨fun h => h.1, fun h => ⟨h, G.ne_of_adj h⟩⟩
621 
622 @[simp] lemma fromEdgeSet_le {s : Set (Sym2 V)} :
623     fromEdgeSet s ≤ G ↔ s \ Sym2.diagSet ⊆ G.edgeSet := by simp [← edgeSet_subset_edgeSet]
624 
625 lemma edgeSet_eq_iff : G.edgeSet = s ↔ G = fromEdgeSet s ∧ Disjoint s Sym2.diagSet where
626   mp := by rintro rfl; simp +contextual [Set.disjoint_right]
627   mpr := by rintro ⟨rfl, hs⟩; simp [hs]
628 
629 @[simp]
630 theorem fromEdgeSet_empty : fromEdgeSet (∅ : Set (Sym2 V)) = ⊥ := by
631   ext v w
632   simp only [fromEdgeSet_adj, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, false_and, bot_adj]
633 
634 @[simp] lemma fromEdgeSet_not_isDiag : @fromEdgeSet V Sym2.diagSetᶜ = ⊤ := by ext; simp
635 
636 @[simp]
637 theorem fromEdgeSet_univ : fromEdgeSet (Set.univ : Set (Sym2 V)) = ⊤ := by
638   ext v w
639   simp only [fromEdgeSet_adj, Set.mem_univ, true_and, top_adj]
640 
641 @[simp]
642 theorem fromEdgeSet_inter (s t : Set (Sym2 V)) :
643     fromEdgeSet (s ∩ t) = fromEdgeSet s ⊓ fromEdgeSet t := by
644   ext v w
645   simp only [fromEdgeSet_adj, Set.mem_inter_iff, Ne, inf_adj]
646   tauto
647 
648 @[simp]
649 theorem fromEdgeSet_union (s t : Set (Sym2 V)) :
650     fromEdgeSet (s ∪ t) = fromEdgeSet s ⊔ fromEdgeSet t := by
651   ext v w
652   simp [Set.mem_union, or_and_right]
653 
654 @[simp]
655 theorem fromEdgeSet_sdiff (s t : Set (Sym2 V)) :
656     fromEdgeSet (s \ t) = fromEdgeSet s \ fromEdgeSet t := by
657   ext v w
658   constructor <;> simp +contextual
659 
660 @[gcongr, mono]
661 theorem fromEdgeSet_mono {s t : Set (Sym2 V)} (h : s ⊆ t) : fromEdgeSet s ≤ fromEdgeSet t := by
662   simpa using Set.diff_subset_diff h fun _ a ↦ a
663 
664 @[simp] lemma disjoint_fromEdgeSet : Disjoint G (fromEdgeSet s) ↔ Disjoint G.edgeSet s := by
665   conv_rhs => rw [← Set.diff_union_inter s Sym2.diagSet]
666   rw [← disjoint_edgeSet, edgeSet_fromEdgeSet]
667   grind [edgeSet_subset_compl_diagSet]
668 
669 @[simp] lemma fromEdgeSet_disjoint : Disjoint (fromEdgeSet s) G ↔ Disjoint s G.edgeSet := by
670   rw [disjoint_comm, disjoint_fromEdgeSet, disjoint_comm]
671 
672 instance [DecidableEq V] [Fintype s] : Fintype (fromEdgeSet s).edgeSet := by
673   rw [edgeSet_fromEdgeSet s]
674   infer_instance
675 
676 end FromEdgeSet
677 
678 theorem disjoint_left {G H : SimpleGraph V} : Disjoint G H ↔ ∀ x y, G.Adj x y → ¬H.Adj x y := by
679   simp [← disjoint_edgeSet, Set.disjoint_left, Sym2.forall]
680 
681 /-! ### Incidence set -/
682 
683 
684 /-- Set of edges incident to a given vertex, aka incidence set. -/
685 def incidenceSet (v : V) : Set (Sym2 V) :=
686   { e ∈ G.edgeSet | v ∈ e }
687 
688 theorem incidenceSet_subset (v : V) : G.incidenceSet v ⊆ G.edgeSet := fun _ h => h.1
689 
690 theorem mk'_mem_incidenceSet_iff : s(b, c) ∈ G.incidenceSet a ↔ G.Adj b c ∧ (a = b ∨ a = c) :=
691   and_congr_right' Sym2.mem_iff
692 
693 theorem mk'_mem_incidenceSet_left_iff : s(a, b) ∈ G.incidenceSet a ↔ G.Adj a b :=
694   and_iff_left <| Sym2.mem_mk_left _ _
695 
696 theorem mk'_mem_incidenceSet_right_iff : s(a, b) ∈ G.incidenceSet b ↔ G.Adj a b :=
697   and_iff_left <| Sym2.mem_mk_right _ _
698 
699 theorem edge_mem_incidenceSet_iff {e : G.edgeSet} : ↑e ∈ G.incidenceSet a ↔ a ∈ (e : Sym2 V) :=
700   and_iff_right e.2
701 
702 theorem incidenceSet_inter_incidenceSet_subset (h : a ≠ b) :
703     G.incidenceSet a ∩ G.incidenceSet b ⊆ {s(a, b)} := fun _e he =>
704   (Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff h).1 ⟨he.1.2, he.2.2⟩
705 
706 theorem incidenceSet_inter_incidenceSet_of_adj (h : G.Adj a b) :
707     G.incidenceSet a ∩ G.incidenceSet b = {s(a, b)} := by
708   refine (G.incidenceSet_inter_incidenceSet_subset <| h.ne).antisymm ?_
709   rintro _ (rfl : _ = s(a, b))
710   exact ⟨G.mk'_mem_incidenceSet_left_iff.2 h, G.mk'_mem_incidenceSet_right_iff.2 h⟩
711 
712 theorem adj_of_mem_incidenceSet (h : a ≠ b) (ha : e ∈ G.incidenceSet a)
713     (hb : e ∈ G.incidenceSet b) : G.Adj a b := by
714   rwa [← mk'_mem_incidenceSet_left_iff, ←
715     Set.mem_singleton_iff.1 <| G.incidenceSet_inter_incidenceSet_subset h ⟨ha, hb⟩]
716 
717 theorem incidenceSet_inter_incidenceSet_of_not_adj (h : ¬G.Adj a b) (hn : a ≠ b) :
718     G.incidenceSet a ∩ G.incidenceSet b = ∅ := by
719   simp_rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem, Set.mem_inter_iff, not_and]
720   intro u ha hb
721   exact h (G.adj_of_mem_incidenceSet hn ha hb)
722 
723 instance decidableMemIncidenceSet [DecidableEq V] [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) :
724     DecidablePred (· ∈ G.incidenceSet v) :=
725   inferInstanceAs <| DecidablePred fun e => e ∈ G.edgeSet ∧ v ∈ e
726 
727 @[simp]
728 theorem mem_neighborSet (v w : V) : w ∈ G.neighborSet v ↔ G.Adj v w :=
729   Iff.rfl
730 
731 lemma notMem_neighborSet_self : a ∉ G.neighborSet a := by simp
732 
733 @[simp]
734 theorem mem_incidenceSet (v w : V) : s(v, w) ∈ G.incidenceSet v ↔ G.Adj v w := by
735   simp [incidenceSet]
736 
737 theorem mem_incidence_iff_neighbor {v w : V} :
738     s(v, w) ∈ G.incidenceSet v ↔ w ∈ G.neighborSet v := by
739   simp only [mem_incidenceSet, mem_neighborSet]
740 
741 theorem adj_incidenceSet_inter {v : V} {e : Sym2 V} (he : e ∈ G.edgeSet) (h : v ∈ e) :
742     G.incidenceSet v ∩ G.incidenceSet (Sym2.Mem.other h) = {e} := by
743   ext e'
744   simp only [incidenceSet, Set.mem_sep_iff, Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
745   refine ⟨fun h' => ?_, ?_⟩
746   · rw [← Sym2.other_spec h]
747     exact (Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff (edge_other_ne G he h).symm).mp ⟨h'.1.2, h'.2.2⟩
748   · rintro rfl
749     exact ⟨⟨he, h⟩, he, Sym2.other_mem _⟩
750 
751 theorem compl_neighborSet_disjoint (G : SimpleGraph V) (v : V) :
752     Disjoint (G.neighborSet v) (Gᶜ.neighborSet v) := by
753   rw [Set.disjoint_iff]
754   rintro w ⟨h, h'⟩
755   rw [mem_neighborSet, compl_adj] at h'
756   exact h'.2 h
757 
758 theorem neighborSet_union_compl_neighborSet_eq (G : SimpleGraph V) (v : V) :
759     G.neighborSet v ∪ Gᶜ.neighborSet v = {v}ᶜ := by
760   ext w
761   have h := @ne_of_adj _ G
762   simp_rw [Set.mem_union, mem_neighborSet, compl_adj, Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
763   tauto
764 
765 theorem card_neighborSet_union_compl_neighborSet [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (v : V)
766     [Fintype (G.neighborSet v ∪ Gᶜ.neighborSet v : Set V)] :
767     #(G.neighborSet v ∪ Gᶜ.neighborSet v).toFinset = Fintype.card V - 1 := by
768   classical simp_rw [neighborSet_union_compl_neighborSet_eq, Set.toFinset_compl,
769       Finset.card_compl, Set.toFinset_card, Set.card_singleton]
770 
771 theorem neighborSet_compl (G : SimpleGraph V) (v : V) :
772     Gᶜ.neighborSet v = (G.neighborSet v)ᶜ \ {v} := by
773   ext w
774   simp [and_comm, eq_comm]
775 
776 /-- The set of common neighbors between two vertices `v` and `w` in a graph `G` is the
777 intersection of the neighbor sets of `v` and `w`. -/
778 def commonNeighbors (v w : V) : Set V :=
779   G.neighborSet v ∩ G.neighborSet w
780 
781 theorem commonNeighbors_eq (v w : V) : G.commonNeighbors v w = G.neighborSet v ∩ G.neighborSet w :=
782   rfl
783 
784 theorem mem_commonNeighbors {u v w : V} : u ∈ G.commonNeighbors v w ↔ G.Adj v u ∧ G.Adj w u :=
785   Iff.rfl
786 
787 theorem commonNeighbors_symm (v w : V) : G.commonNeighbors v w = G.commonNeighbors w v :=
788   Set.inter_comm _ _
789 
790 theorem notMem_commonNeighbors_left (v w : V) : v ∉ G.commonNeighbors v w := fun h =>
791   ne_of_adj G h.1 rfl
792 
793 theorem notMem_commonNeighbors_right (v w : V) : w ∉ G.commonNeighbors v w := fun h =>
794   ne_of_adj G h.2 rfl
795 
796 theorem commonNeighbors_subset_neighborSet_left (v w : V) :
797     G.commonNeighbors v w ⊆ G.neighborSet v :=
798   Set.inter_subset_left
799 
800 theorem commonNeighbors_subset_neighborSet_right (v w : V) :
801     G.commonNeighbors v w ⊆ G.neighborSet w :=
802   Set.inter_subset_right
803 
804 instance decidableMemCommonNeighbors [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v w : V) :
805     DecidablePred (· ∈ G.commonNeighbors v w) :=
806   inferInstanceAs <| DecidablePred fun u => u ∈ G.neighborSet v ∧ u ∈ G.neighborSet w
807 
808 theorem commonNeighbors_top_eq {v w : V} :
809     (⊤ : SimpleGraph V).commonNeighbors v w = Set.univ \ {v, w} := by
810   ext u
811   simp [commonNeighbors, eq_comm, not_or]
812 
813 section Incidence
814 
815 variable [DecidableEq V]
816 
817 /-- Given an edge incident to a particular vertex, get the other vertex on the edge. -/
818 def otherVertexOfIncident {v : V} {e : Sym2 V} (h : e ∈ G.incidenceSet v) : V :=
819   Sym2.Mem.other' h.2
820 
821 theorem edge_other_incident_set {v : V} {e : Sym2 V} (h : e ∈ G.incidenceSet v) :
822     e ∈ G.incidenceSet (G.otherVertexOfIncident h) := by
823   use h.1
824   simp [otherVertexOfIncident, Sym2.other_mem']
825 
826 theorem incidence_other_prop {v : V} {e : Sym2 V} (h : e ∈ G.incidenceSet v) :
827     G.otherVertexOfIncident h ∈ G.neighborSet v := by
828   obtain ⟨he, hv⟩ := h
829   rwa [← Sym2.other_spec' hv, mem_edgeSet] at he
830 
831 @[simp]
832 theorem incidence_other_neighbor_edge {v w : V} (h : w ∈ G.neighborSet v) :
833     G.otherVertexOfIncident (G.mem_incidence_iff_neighbor.mpr h) = w :=
834   Sym2.congr_right.mp (Sym2.other_spec' (G.mem_incidence_iff_neighbor.mpr h).right)
835 
836 /-- There is an equivalence between the set of edges incident to a given
837 vertex and the set of vertices adjacent to the vertex. -/
838 @[simps]
839 def incidenceSetEquivNeighborSet (v : V) : G.incidenceSet v ≃ G.neighborSet v where
840   toFun e := ⟨G.otherVertexOfIncident e.2, G.incidence_other_prop e.2⟩
841   invFun w := ⟨s(v, w.1), G.mem_incidence_iff_neighbor.mpr w.2⟩
842   left_inv x := by simp [otherVertexOfIncident]
843   right_inv := fun ⟨w, hw⟩ => by
844     simp only [Subtype.mk.injEq]
845     exact incidence_other_neighbor_edge _ hw
846 
847 end Incidence
848 
849 section IsCompleteBetween
850 
851 variable {s t : Set V}
852 
853 /-- The condition that the portion of the simple graph `G` _between_ `s` and `t` is complete, that
854 is, every vertex in `s` is adjacent to every vertex in `t`, and vice versa. -/
855 def IsCompleteBetween (G : SimpleGraph V) (s t : Set V) :=
856   ∀ ⦃v₁⦄, v₁ ∈ s → ∀ ⦃v₂⦄, v₂ ∈ t → G.Adj v₁ v₂
857 
858 theorem IsCompleteBetween.disjoint (h : G.IsCompleteBetween s t) : Disjoint s t :=
859   Set.disjoint_left.mpr fun v hv₁ hv₂ ↦ (G.loopless.irrefl v) (h hv₁ hv₂)
860 
861 theorem isCompleteBetween_comm : G.IsCompleteBetween s t ↔ G.IsCompleteBetween t s where
862   mp h _ h₁ _ h₂ := (h h₂ h₁).symm
863   mpr h _ h₁ _ h₂ := (h h₂ h₁).symm
864 
865 alias ⟨IsCompleteBetween.symm, _⟩ := isCompleteBetween_comm
866 
867 end IsCompleteBetween
868 
869 section Subsingleton
870 
871 protected theorem subsingleton_iff : Subsingleton (SimpleGraph V) ↔ Subsingleton V := by
872   refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, fun _ ↦ Unique.instSubsingleton⟩
873   contrapose! h
874   exact instNontrivial
875 
876 protected theorem nontrivial_iff : Nontrivial (SimpleGraph V) ↔ Nontrivial V := by
877   refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, fun _ ↦ instNontrivial⟩
878   contrapose! h
879   exact Unique.instSubsingleton
880 
881 end Subsingleton
882 
883 end SimpleGraph
